agents.name: Claude Code
agents.context_note: AGENTS.md is read directly from v2.1.277; where it is not available, a CLAUDE.md that imports it covers the same ground.
agents.limits: Project instruction loading is configurable, so which file an agent reads depends on a setting the catalog cannot see.

agents.name: Codex CLI
agents.context_note: Instructions are read from ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, then each AGENTS.md on the way down to the working directory; AGENTS.override.md replaces broader guidance for one subtree.
agents.limits: Project-scoped .codex/config.toml only loads in a trusted directory; the first encounter in an untrusted one prompts before any server starts.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
agents.context_note: Repository instructions are included automatically for prompts entered in that repository.
agents.limits: Ships with the GitHub MCP server already configured; servers live in ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json. Grant tools individually with --allow-tool rather than --allow-all-tools.

agents.name: Cursor
agents.context_note: A rule file needs YAML frontmatter with description, globs and alwaysApply; a plain .md in .cursor/rules has none and is ignored. Nested AGENTS.md files apply to their own subtree, most specific first.
agents.limits: An editor, not a CLI: setup recipes that assume a terminal agent have to be run by the user. MCP servers are added through the settings UI.

agents.name: Gemini CLI
agents.context_note: The context file name is the `context.fileName` setting and takes a list, so AGENTS.md can be added alongside GEMINI.md rather than replacing it.
agents.limits: Environment variables are expanded in the config with $VAR or ${VAR}, and %VAR% on Windows only.

agents.name: Windsurf
agents.context_note: Rule files carry a `trigger` frontmatter field — always_on, model_decision, glob or manual. A root AGENTS.md has no frontmatter and is always on.
agents.limits: Workspace rule files are capped at 12,000 characters and global ones at 6,000, so a long AGENTS.md is silently truncated. OAuth is unavailable for stdio servers. Documentation now redirects to docs.devin.ai and the config path has moved with it; the legacy path was ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json.

agents.name: Cline
agents.context_note: Reads a workspace AGENTS.md and a cross-tool ~/.agents/AGENTS.md as the standard format for compatibility with other agents.
agents.limits: MCP servers live in ~/.cline/mcp.json for the CLI and in the panel for the extensions. SSE is legacy; use streamableHttp for new servers.

agents.name: OpenCode
agents.context_note: AGENTS.md is preferred and CLAUDE.md is the fallback; the first match wins per category. `instructions` in opencode.json adds more files, and accepts globs and remote URLs.
agents.limits: MCP servers are declared in opencode.json under `mcp` with type local or remote; there is no add subcommand, the file is edited.

agents.name: Kiro
agents.context_note: Steering files use an `inclusion` frontmatter field — always, fileMatch, manual or auto — which must be the first content in the file. An AGENTS.md needs no inclusion mode and is always included.
agents.limits: MCP servers live in .kiro/settings/mcp.json, and an environment variable is only expanded after it is added to the approved-variables setting.

experts.name: DevOps Platform Engineer
experts.summary: Pin by digest, give the build least privilege, make rollback a tested path, and define the SLO before the dashboard.

experts.name: .NET Senior Software Architect
experts.summary: Decide the expensive things first, hold the dependency direction, and refuse the eleven patterns that are structural to remove.

experts.name: Frontend Engineer
experts.summary: Build web UI to targets somebody can measure — WCAG 2.2 AA, Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile, a declared Baseline and a byte budget — and claim nothing a check did not show.

experts.name: Performance Engineer
experts.summary: Measure first, change one thing, measure again — and a result smaller than the run-to-run spread is not a result.

experts.name: Product Manager
experts.summary: The problem before the solution, a metric that could come back negative, criteria somebody could fail, and what is not being built.

experts.name: QA Automation Lead
experts.summary: Test the behaviour, make it deterministic, treat a flaky test as a failed one, and keep the signal worth acting on.

experts.name: Security Reviewer
experts.summary: Boundaries first, then authorization. Every finding cites a control at a version, or it is an opinion and stays out.

experts.name: SQL Data Engineer
experts.summary: Model first, migrate in three deploys rather than one, index because a query asked, and assume every load runs twice.

experts.name: Technical Program Manager
experts.summary: Split work across agents only when the plan is wide enough to repay it, freeze the interfaces first, and never let a worker mark its own work done.

experts.name: Technical Writer
experts.summary: Decide the document's type before its first sentence, write for the reader's task, run every sample, and delete more than you add.

crews.name: API Hardening Crew
crews.summary: Three specialists for an API that already has users, where the job is finding what is wrong rather than deciding what to build.
crews.for_what: Hardening an API that is already in production: finding the authorization gaps, making the suite worth gating on, and turning a rollback from a belief into a tested path.
crews.not_for: A greenfield project, where there is nothing to harden yet and the decisions worth taking are architectural rather than defensive.

crews.name: SaaS Launch Crew
crews.summary: The four specialists a multi-tenant SaaS needs before its first customer, and the two integrations they all reach for.
crews.for_what: Taking a multi-tenant SaaS from an empty repository to a first paying customer, where the decisions that are expensive to reverse are taken before there is data to migrate.
crews.not_for: A prototype, an internal tool, or anything single-tenant. Four experts on a project with no customers is four opinions nobody has time to reconcile.

integrations.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
integrations.summary: Read the console, the network log and a performance trace from a running Chrome, from an agent.

install.codex: codex mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.10.1 --no-usage-statistics
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add chrome-devtools npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.10.1 --no-usage-statistics

integrations.permissions_summary: Drives a Chrome instance: navigates, runs JavaScript in its pages, and reads their console, network traffic and performance traces.

integrations.name: Context7
integrations.summary: Library documentation at the version in use, fetched on demand instead of recalled from training.
integrations.permissions_summary: Sends the library name and your query to Context7's service and returns documentation.

integrations.name: Exa Search MCP
integrations.summary: Web search built for agents: results as content rather than as a list of links to fetch.

install.codex: codex mcp add exa --env EXA_API_KEY=$EXA_API_KEY -- npx -y exa-mcp-server@3.4.1
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add exa -e 'EXA_API_KEY=${EXA_API_KEY}' npx -y exa-mcp-server@3.4.1

integrations.permissions_summary: Sends your search query to Exa's service and returns page content.

integrations.name: Figma Context MCP
integrations.summary: Read a Figma file's layout and styles as structured data, so generated UI matches the design.

install.codex: codex mcp add figma --env FIGMA_API_KEY=$FIGMA_API_KEY -- npx -y figma-developer-mcp@0.13.2 --stdio
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add figma -e FIGMA_API_KEY=$FIGMA_API_KEY npx -y figma-developer-mcp@0.13.2 --stdio

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads the Figma files the access token can reach, through Figma's API.

integrations.name: Filesystem MCP
integrations.summary: Read and write files under directories named on the command line, and nowhere else.
integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes every file under the directories passed as arguments, with the privileges of the user running it.

integrations.name: GitHub MCP Server
integrations.summary: Issues, pull requests, Actions and code search on the repositories a token can reach.

install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --transport http --header "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes every repository the token can reach: issues, pull requests, workflow runs and file contents.

integrations.name: Memory MCP
integrations.summary: A local knowledge graph an agent writes to and reads back across sessions.
integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes a knowledge graph in a local file; reaches nothing else.

integrations.name: Notion MCP
integrations.summary: Read and write the Notion pages and databases an integration token has been granted.

install.codex: codex mcp add notion --env NOTION_TOKEN=$NOTION_TOKEN -- npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server@2.5.2
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add notion -e NOTION_TOKEN=$NOTION_TOKEN npx -y @notionhq/notion-mcp-server@2.5.2

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads and writes the pages and databases explicitly shared with the integration.

integrations.name: Playwright MCP
integrations.summary: Drive a real browser from an agent: navigate, fill, click and read the accessibility tree.
integrations.permissions_summary: Launches a browser on this machine and visits whatever the agent asks it to, including local services.

integrations.name: Sentry MCP
integrations.summary: Read issues, events and stack traces from Sentry, so an agent debugs from the real error.

install.codex: codex mcp add sentry --env SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN=$SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN -- npx -y @sentry/mcp-server@0.40.0
install.gemini-cli: gemini mcp add sentry -e SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN=$SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN npx -y @sentry/mcp-server@0.40.0

integrations.permissions_summary: Reads issues, events and stack traces, and can update issues (assign, unassign, resolve), in the Sentry organisations the token can reach.
